name: @w6w-apps/google-forms
description: Create and update Google Forms, manage publish state, and read form responses.

w6w.longDescription:
Google Forms creates and updates forms, manages whether a form is published and accepting responses, and reads back the responses submitted to it, against Google's own Forms API. A form is created with just a title, then built up through explicit follow-up updates — adding, moving and deleting items, and updating form settings — since Google's own create call accepts nothing beyond a title to begin with.

Items — questions, page breaks, images, videos and grading — are passed through as the API's own structured JSON rather than flattened into a simplified field set, so the full range of question and grading options stays available without a second schema to maintain. Because items are addressed by position rather than by a stable id, moving or deleting one is treated as non-repeatable: running it twice acts on whatever now sits at that position, not the original item.

A user's own Google sign-in covers personal forms, while a service account handles unattended, server-to-server runs — with the caveat that a form a service account creates has no owner who can open it in Drive unless ownership is handed to a real user afterward. Listing existing forms and reading responses round out the read side; watch subscriptions and quiz grading are left out, since the former needs infrastructure this app can't provide and the latter is already reachable through the same item JSON.
